headline: How a CAD Drafting Firm Tripled Its Google Ads Leads on a Flat Budget
summary_line: PPC Guru launched and scaled a CAD drafting and permit-drawing firm's Google Ads from the ground up. Holding monthly budget essentially flat at around $2,900, the account grew from 18 genuine calls and form leads in its first month to roughly 55 a month in the most recent quarter (Apr–Jun 2026) — cutting cost per lead from about $162 to about $51 through structure and search-term discipline, not extra spend.
client_context: The client is a CAD drafting and engineering-drawing firm serving the Greater Toronto Area, producing technical drawings and city-permit drawing packages for renovation and construction projects. Its enquiries come from property owners, contractors and builders searching for drafting and permit help — high-intent phone calls and form submissions. Google Ads is the firm's primary channel for capturing that demand at the moment people are looking for a drafter.
background: The firm partnered with PPC Guru to build its Google Ads presence from scratch in January 2023. Rather than starting small and ramping, the account launched at a full working budget of around $2,900 a month, with the goal of turning search demand for drafting and permit drawings into a predictable flow of enquiries. From day one the brief was clear: measurable calls and form leads, not just clicks.
analysis: PPC Guru built the account around the two highest-value demand pockets — general drafting services and city-permit drawings for the GTA — and wired up genuine call and lead-form tracking before optimising. Early months deliberately cast a wide net to gather search-term data; the work from there was disciplined refinement: cutting irrelevant queries, concentrating budget on converting searches, and letting Maximize Conversions bidding compound the gains.
analysis_points: Launch dedicated Search campaigns for drafting services and city-permit drawings (GTA).
Track genuine phone calls and lead-form submissions, including a dedicated permit-offer landing page.
Mine early search-term data and build out negatives to cut wasted clicks.
Run Maximize Conversions bidding and let cost per lead fall as the data matured — without raising budget.

timeline.what: Launch month — 18 genuine call and form leads at about $162 each, on a ~$2,900 budget.
First full quarter — about 84 leads (roughly 28 a month) as early search-term data came in.
Steady volume around 50–60 leads a month as negatives and structure tightened.
Consistent lead flow on the same flat budget, cost per lead holding well below launch levels.
About 55 genuine leads a month at roughly $51 each — cost per lead cut by about two-thirds versus launch.

challenge: Building a new account for a specialised service is a cold start: no historical conversion data, and drafting and permit searches sit alongside plenty of loosely related queries. Early on the campaigns drew heavy traffic — several thousand clicks a month — at a cost per lead north of $160. The challenge was to convert that raw traffic into qualified drafting and permit enquiries and drive the cost per lead down, all without increasing the monthly budget.

changes.why: Separating general drafting from city-permit drawings let each get the right message, keywords and budget share.
Measured real phone calls and lead-form submissions — including a dedicated permit-offer page — instead of counting button clicks.
Early broad traffic (up to ~4,800 clicks/mo) was pruned with negatives so budget reached genuine drafting intent.
With clean lead data, automated bidding steadily lowered cost per lead on the same spend.
Growth came from efficiency, not more money — the same ~$2,900 a month produced roughly three times the leads.

benchmark: All figures are genuine phone-call and lead-form conversions; Google local actions and click-to-call taps on the Business Profile are excluded. Because the monthly budget was essentially unchanged from launch to now, the fall in cost per lead — from about $162 to about $51 — reflects sharper targeting and bidding rather than extra spend.

early_stage.title: The First 90 Days
early_stage.intro: The account launched at full budget and immediately produced measurable leads, then improved fast as search-term data accumulated. Cost per lead more than halved between the first and third month as negatives took hold.

gradual: From that fast start the account settled into a dependable rhythm. Through 2024 it held around 50–60 genuine leads a month, and it has stayed in that band through 2025 and into 2026 — all on the same flat budget. The monthly trend below shows the natural variation of a real account around a consistent, efficient baseline, with cost per lead holding far below where it launched.

spotlight.title: Why a Flat Budget Tells the Real Story
spotlight.body: It is easy to grow leads by spending more. This account did the opposite: monthly budget barely moved from launch to today, yet leads roughly tripled and cost per lead fell by about two-thirds. That gap is the value of the management itself — every additional lead came from better keyword targeting, tighter negatives and smarter bidding, not a bigger cheque. For a specialised drafting and permit business, that efficiency is what makes the channel sustainable.

lessons: A new account is a data-gathering exercise first — expect a higher cost per lead in month one and judge it on the trend.
Separate distinct services (general drafting vs permit drawings) so each gets the right keywords and budget.
Negatives are where the savings live — prune irrelevant searches relentlessly in the early months.
Track genuine calls and form submissions, not button clicks, so bidding optimises toward real enquiries.
More leads don't require more budget — efficiency on a flat spend is often the bigger win.
why_it_worked: Two focused Search campaigns matched budget to the firm's highest-value services.
Genuine call and form tracking let bidding optimise toward real enquiries from launch.
Disciplined search-term and negative-keyword work drove cost per lead down over time.
Growth came from efficiency on a flat budget, making the channel sustainable.
outcome: Today the firm runs a predictable Google Ads program that turns GTA search demand for drafting and permit drawings into a steady flow of enquiries. In the most recent complete quarter (April–June 2026) the account generated about 55 genuine call and form leads a month at roughly $51 each — up from 18 leads at about $162 each in its launch month, on essentially the same budget. With cost per lead cut by about two-thirds through management alone, the firm has a dependable, efficient channel it can rely on.

methodology: All figures are pulled directly from the client's Google Ads account and shown on a monthly basis. 'Leads' are genuine phone calls and lead-form submissions only; Google local actions and click-to-call taps are excluded. 'Then' is the first complete month under management (January 2023); 'Now' is the most recent complete quarter (April–June 2026). Monthly budget was essentially flat across the whole period.
lead_quality: Leads are a mix of direct phone calls and website lead-form submissions, including enquiries from a dedicated permit-drawing offer page — both high-intent actions for a drafting and permit business.
